channel_name: Los Angeles County - Board of Supervisors
title: Sybil Brand Commission for Institutional Inspections (SBC) February 5, 2026 Meeting
description:
The Sybil Brand Commission for Institutional Inspections (SBC) meeting of February 5, 2026 highlighted the alarming number of in custody deaths reported in 2026 and reinforced the SBCs mandate to monitor jail conditions and pursue accountability.

The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department (LASD) reported out on meals, water quality, food waste, and facility equipment postponed to March 2026, limiting immediate insight into key operational areas. A discussion ensued with District Attorney Nathan Hochman on the handling of sexual assault allegations involving deputies, systemic failures in facilities such as the Century Regional Detention Facility (CRDF), and the deteriorating conditions of Men’s Central Jail (MCJ). Hochman expressed support for the SBC’s oversight role and affirmed the DA’s commitment to independent investigation of misconduct, while also noting the ongoing need for structural reform and facility replacement.

The SBC raised concerns about violence, retaliation, Title 15 violations, and lack of transparency, particularly regarding the so called “cop shop” allegations. And the necessity of obtaining consistent corrective action plan (CAP) responses and strengthening inter agency cooperation.

The LASD’s Prison Rape Elimination Act (PREA) Coordinator, explained complaint intake, investigative pathways, and the roles of specialized units. Despite these updates, the SBC underscored the need for robust accountability measures and clearer communication from LASDs leadership.
